title: Romeo and Juliet
text:
In Verona, two noble families, the Montagues and the Capulets, had been feuding for so long that no one remembered how it started. Their servants brawled in the streets, and the Prince warned that the next fight would cost lives.

Romeo, a young Montague, slipped into a Capulet party and fell in love with Juliet, the Capulets' thirteen-year-old daughter. Only afterward did each learn the other's name. That night, under her balcony, they declared their love, and the next day Friar Laurence married them in secret, hoping the match might end the feud.

Within hours Juliet's cousin Tybalt killed Romeo's friend Mercutio, and Romeo, enraged, killed Tybalt. He was banished. Juliet's parents, knowing nothing of the marriage, ordered her to marry Count Paris at once and threatened to throw her out if she refused.

The friar gave Juliet a potion that would make her seem dead for two days, and sent word to Romeo. The message never reached him. Hearing only that Juliet was dead, Romeo bought poison, went to her tomb and drank it beside her. Juliet woke, found him dead, and stabbed herself with his dagger.

Over the bodies of their children, the two fathers finally clasped hands and ended the feud.
lesson: Quarrels between families do not stay with the people who start them. Children inherit them and pay for them. End the feud before they must.
people: Romeo, Juliet, the Montagues and Capulets, Friar Laurence, Tybalt
location: Verona, Italy (play written in London, England)
